## The question

Landed cost models start as one spreadsheet and end as a file only one person
can safely edit — freight allocated by weight in one column, by value in
another, tariff rates hardcoded, and no way to see the version that produced
last quarter's decision.

The question is what the same calculation looks like as a normalized schema, and
what that buys.

## Approach

Third normal form, then landed cost as a view rather than a stored column, so
the calculation has one definition.

[Add the ER diagram — Quarto renders Mermaid natively:]

```{mermaid}
%%| eval: false
erDiagram
    VENDOR ||--o{ PURCHASE_ORDER : places
    PURCHASE_ORDER ||--|{ PO_LINE : contains
    SKU ||--o{ PO_LINE : "appears on"
    SKU }o--|| HTS_CODE : "classified as"
    HTS_CODE ||--o{ DUTY_RATE : "has rate by origin"
    SHIPMENT ||--|{ PO_LINE : carries
    SHIPMENT }o--|| FREIGHT_QUOTE : priced_by
```

The allocation rule is the interesting decision: freight and insurance are
charged per shipment but landed cost is needed per unit, so the cost has to be
apportioned. [Say which basis you chose — weight, value, or volume — and what it
does to per-unit cost for dense cheap goods versus light expensive ones. That
choice changes which SKUs look profitable.]

```{sql}
#| eval: false
create view landed_cost as
select l.po_line_id,
       s.sku_code,
       l.unit_price,
       l.unit_price * d.rate                        as duty_per_unit,
       f.total_cost * (l.line_weight_kg
                       / sh.total_weight_kg)
                    / l.quantity                    as freight_per_unit
from po_line       l
join sku           s  on s.sku_id = l.sku_id
join hts_code      h  on h.hts_id = s.hts_id
join duty_rate     d  on d.hts_id = h.hts_id
                     and d.origin_country = l.origin_country
join shipment      sh on sh.shipment_id = l.shipment_id
join freight_quote f  on f.quote_id = sh.quote_id;
```

## What I found

[Compare the two approaches on something concrete: how many SKUs change rank on
landed cost when the allocation basis changes from value to weight, and what
that would mean for a sourcing decision.]

## What I would do differently

[Candidates: duty rates need effective dates so historical entries reprice
correctly, currency is assumed constant, and a real model needs to handle
partial shipments and split orders.]
